title: Two integral forms of the Kullback–Leibler divergence
statement:
Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be probability measures on a measurable space $\Omega$ with $\mu$ absolutely continuous with respect to $
u$, and write $ rac{d\mu}{d
u}$ for the (real-valued) Radon–Nikodym density of $\mu$ with respect to $
u$. Assume that the log-likelihood ratio $x \mapsto \log rac{d\mu}{d
u}(x)$ is $\mu$-integrable. Then
\[
  \int_\Omega \varphi\!\left( rac{d\mu}{d
u}(x)ight) d
u(x)
  \;=\;
  \int_\Omega \log rac{d\mu}{d
u}(x)\, d\mu(x),
\]
where $\varphi(t) = t\log t + 1 - t$.
hypotheses_covered: $\mu$ and $\nu$ are probability measures on a measurable space $\Omega$
$\mu$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $\nu$ ($\mu \ll \nu$)
